result.topic_en: A table of river depths against the minimum slope per 1000 feet needed for flow, followed by the formula for the river's velocity when the slope exceeds the tabulated value, and the start of a new case of water flowing from a vessel through a horizontal tube.

93. Si ergo decliuitas pro data profunditate maior fuerit, quam haec tabula indicat, aqua in alueo decurret; eiusque celeritas proxime innotescet, si ponatur $g=1$, vnde fiet:
$$v = a + (e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}} - 1)(\tfrac{1}{\alpha} g \cos.\zeta - l)$$
Patet ergo, manente eadem decliuitate, ita tamen, vt $\cos.\zeta > \frac{\alpha l}{g}$, celeritatem fluminis eo fore maiorem, quo longior fuerit fluuii tractus. Notari etiam conuenit, cursum fluuii eiusdem accelerari, si pondus atmosphaerae diminuatur.

94. Quoniam ante (86, 87) casum euoluimus, quo aqua ex vase, centum pedes alto, ad distantiam centum pedum per tubum horizontalem, cuius amplitudo $gg = \frac{1}{100}$ ped. erat deriuata; ponamus nunc eiusdem vasis altitudinem esse minimam, ex eoque aquam

items.quote: Si ergo decliuitas pro data profunditate maior fuerit, quam haec tabula indicat, aqua in alueo decurret; eiusque celeritas proxime innotescet, si ponatur $g=1$
items.english: If therefore the slope for a given depth is greater than this table indicates, the water will flow down the channel, and its velocity will be approximately known by setting $g=1$.

items.quote: Patet ergo, manente eadem decliuitate, ita tamen, vt $\cos.\zeta > \frac{\alpha l}{g}$, celeritatem fluminis eo fore maiorem, quo longior fuerit fluuii tractus.
items.english: It is therefore clear that, with the slope unchanged but such that $\cos\zeta > \alpha l/g$, the velocity of the river will be greater the longer the river's course.

items.quote: Notari etiam conuenit, cursum fluuii eiusdem accelerari, si pondus atmosphaerae diminuatur.
items.english: It should also be noted that the flow of the same river is accelerated if the weight of the atmosphere decreases.

items.quote: ponamus nunc eiusdem vasis altitudinem esse minimam, ex eoque aquam
items.english: Let us now suppose the height of the same vessel to be very small, and the water from it [to be led] ...
